public_body: Massachusetts Board Of Elementary And Secondary Education
overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the May 24 notice described both topics with sufficient specificity, and attachments and advance distribution of documents to the public are not required.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the May 24 meeting notice failed to include attachments corresponding to two listed topics (Boston Public Schools update and SSAC year-end report).
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require that a public body attach supporting documents to a meeting notice or that it publicly post a “meeting packet” that contains such documents.

allegations.summary: Whether the two topics, Boston Public Schools update and SSAC year-end report, were described with sufficient specificity in the posted notice.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the notice for the Board’s May 24 meeting described the two topics at issue, Boston Public Schools Update and State Student Advisory Council Year End Report, with sufficient specificity.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board violated public access rights by giving the two documents to outside stakeholders around May 19 but not posting them to the public until May 23.
allegations.key_passage: As stated above, there is no requirement in the Open Meeting Law that the public body affirmatively provide copies of documents to persons in attendance at a meeting.
